grh_e0fa7b6bc929e1c13bcc.title: Britt Ponsett's Christmas Carol
paragraphs: On Christmas Eve Britt meets a runaway boy who insists that Christmas is only for children and that he wants nothing to do with it. To keep him company, Britt retells A Christmas Carol as a Western tale about wealthy miser Evan, whose dead partner and a succession of visions force him to confront the lonely life his greed has created and inspire him to become generous. The story, along with a little discreet gift-giving by Britt, helps the boy reconsider the gruff relative caring for him and turn back toward home. Britt leaves the pair with presents and a renewed chance to celebrate Christmas together.

Other credited names include Jack Johnstone as director, Jack Johnstone as producer, Frank Burt as writer, and Hal Gibney as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Britt Ponset]].

grh_e0b81e9455e11a9585c4.title: Incident at Red Butte
paragraphs: Overland stage boss Russell has built a frontier legend by keeping his Wyoming division running through outlaw country, but the men around him begin to see the brutality behind his reputation. Jenny tries to escape him, and young Seth initially refuses to believe her stories until he watches Russell execute suspected horse thieves without trial and nearly burn a cheating hay seller alive. Seth finally defies Russell, helps a stranded family and prepares to leave with Jenny. Russell forces a gun confrontation, and Seth shoots him, concluding that whatever good man Russell may once have been was lost long before the final showdown.
